title: "Overview"

## Publishing is more than a paper

Research does not end with a paper. Data, code, and other research outputs are
valuable parts of the work and should be preserved, discoverable, and reusable,
making them [FAIR](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/). Sharing them
should be a natural part of publishing --- not an extra burden.

A paper tells others what you found; the data, code, methods, and workflows can
help others understand, verify, reproduce, and build on it. Making these outputs
available also reduces duplicated effort and allows research to travel further
than its original publication.

## Why Zenodo?

[Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/) provides a safe and persistent home for research
outputs. It preserves files and metadata, makes them discoverable, and gives
published records a DOI so they can be cited and reused. Zenodo is recommended
as the open repository for EU-funded research outputs and can also be used for
pre-registrations of research articles. It also has a very nice programmatic
interface, which makes it easier to develop tools that simplify working with
Zenodo.

## Why use zen-do?

The overall aim of the [Seedcase Project](https://seedcase-project.org) is to
build tools that make data more
[FAIR](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/), easier to access and share,
and more likely to be (re)used. However, a secondary aim of Seedcase is to build
tools that make it easier to do open science. To support this goal, zen-do
simplifies specific tasks related to disseminating different scientific output.

### Being FAIR should be easy

Publishing to Zenodo should not require learning another web interface or
managing the same information in several places. zen-do provides a command-line
interface (CLI) for preparing, managing, converting, and publishing Zenodo
deposits from a metadata file and your existing research files.

Publishing research outputs to Zenodo with zen-do makes it an easy part of your
normal research workflow. It provides a simple way to keep the information about
a deposit together with the work it describes, manage changes along the way, and
publish when everything is ready.

The goal is to remove the small but persistent obstacles that make sharing
research feel like extra work: keeping metadata consistent, handling files,
tracking drafts, and repeating steps through a web interface.

With zen-do, publishing becomes something you can prepare, update, and reproduce
alongside your research.

## Learning more

This website contains a guide on how to use zen-do, reference documentation, and
details about the design:

- [How-to guide](/docs/guide/index.qmd): The guide section provides a
  step-by-step introduction to zen-do, including installing the CLI and using
  it.
- [Reference](/docs/reference/index.qmd): The reference section contains
  detailed information about zen-do's CLI and its Rust library.
- [Design](/docs/design/index.qmd): The design section describes the
  architecture and interface of zen-do, the requirements, use-cases, and [C4
  model](https://c4model.com/) diagrams.
